name: Geolibertarianism
summary: Geolibertarianism combines libertarian non-aggression and free markets with the Georgist view that land and natural resources are a common inheritance. People own what their labor produces, but those who hold land owe the community its rental value, which replaces taxes on labor, goods and income and funds minimal government and often an equal dividend to all.
scope: The mainstream strand coined by Fred Foldvary in 1981: land-rent public finance within a limited-government libertarian framework, drawing on Locke, Paine's Agrarian Justice and Henry George's Progress and Poverty. Foldvary's geoanarchism (private rent-collecting agencies, no state) is treated as a minority variant; non-libertarian Georgism and Rothbardian libertarians who reject land rent are excluded.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: George holds wages rise by freeing land and untaxing labor, not by wage mandates; libertarian side opposes price-fixing.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Geolibertarians pair free markets with land-rent public finance, trusting markets for produced goods and services.

public-ownership.rationale: Only land rent is publicly collected; industries stay private under the libertarian side of the synthesis.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Revenue should come from land rent, not from taxing produced wealth or income, so no general wealth tax.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property in what labor produces is sacred, yet land is held subject to a rent owed to the community.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Libertarian minimal-state outlook opposes tighter regulation, favoring rent and pollution charges instead.

cut-welfare.rationale: They favor replacing bureaucratic welfare with an unconditional rent dividend, so adherents are split on simply cutting.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership structure is for voluntary choice; mandated collective ownership conflicts with libertarian principle.

state-harmful.rationale: Mainstream geolibertarians keep a minimal state funded by land rent; only the geoanarchist strand abolishes it.

decide-locally.rationale: Foldvary funds local public goods from local geo-rent and favors small voluntary associations and cellular democracy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Crimes are defined by victims, but the sources do not choose between restitution, punishment and rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Indifferent on family form; the ideology is about land and liberty.

abortion-legal.rationale: Libertarians split on abortion and the sources are silent.

gradual-change.rationale: Foldvary proposes phasing in rent from 25 percent to 75 percent over twenty years, indicating gradualism in transition.

free-trade.rationale: Libertarian core favors free trade, and taxes on goods are among those to be abolished in favor of land rent.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether revolution is sometimes justified, and this disagreement rested on a preference for reform or lawful means, which doesn't say revolution is never justified.

reviewHistory.rationale: Reform by tax shift is the aim; Paine defended revolution against tyranny but the ideology proposes policy change.

central-planning.rationale: Libertarian core rejects planning in favor of markets.

socialized-markets.rationale: Accepts markets, but ownership form is left to voluntary choice, not conditioned on public or worker ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Central policy: tax land's rental value, untax labor, buildings, sales and income.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Paine proposed an inheritance levy, but the modern synthesis taxes land rent rather than bequests of produced wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Surplus rent is distributed equally to each citizen as a dividend, though geoanarchists pay it via private agencies rather than the state.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Taxes on trade and goods are rejected by both the libertarian and Georgist strands.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Libertarian opposition to state economic direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: George wanted land value shared by all, not necessarily dispersed plots; produced wealth distribution is left to markets.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wages are protected and untaxed in their program.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-fixed wages and prices contradict libertarian markets.

one-party-rule.rationale: Equal liberty and limited government are incompatible with single-party rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Foldvary proposes alternative democratic forms and voluntary associations; adherents ambivalent on majority rule.

right-to-secede.rationale: Geoanarchism lets individuals leave a geocommunity and forgo its services.

natural-rulers.rationale: Paine and Georgist egalitarianism hold natural equality of birthright.

war-builds-character.rationale: Non-aggression and peace oriented; war is rejected.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law of equal liberty, not scripture, underlies law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Geoanarchists accept private protection and law, while mainstream geolibertarians keep a minimal state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Universal equal-rights tradition rejects ethnic definitions of nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: George saw landowners versus labor, not class conflict as history's engine, and sought harmony.

equal-outcomes.rationale: People own what they produce; only land rent is shared equally.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Natural rights tradition from Locke and Paine puts rights first.

limit-population.rationale: George rejected population pressure as the root of poverty and no coercive limits are proposed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: George held progress yields wealth, with poverty caused by land monopoly, not industry.

restore-past-order.rationale: The program is a reform toward a new rent system, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: A principled, natural-rights ideology rather than pragmatism.

return-to-foraging.rationale: George links progress with wealth; rejects return to primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Market exchange and specialization are core to the libertarian side.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Dividend is equal, and produced goods belong to producers.

profit-exploitation.rationale: George located exploitation in rent, not in profit or interest.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Opposed to dictatorship and class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Private use of land under rent payment, not collective farms.

taxation-theft.rationale: Geolibertarians treat rent as owed to the community but split on whether other taxes are theft.

harm-principle.rationale: The law of equal liberty and victim-defined crimes underlie the ideology.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Libertarian individualism, though land belongs to all equally.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Geoanarchism gives voluntary exit from geocommunities as the central check.

state-as-business.rationale: Foldvary notes government collecting rent has incentive to improve neighborhoods, like a landlord firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Libertarian stress on non-interference; George stresses access to land as the base of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a theme in the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equal natural rights tradition; no support in the sources.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not part of a liberal-libertarian framework.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal rule contradicts equal birthright claims.

bound-labor.rationale: Paine and George oppose land monopoly binding labor.

universal-morality.rationale: Paine and Locke ground rights in universal natural law.

single-common-good.rationale: Individualist liberalism rather than a single common good.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Mandated voting in private firms conflicts with property and contract.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarian premise that liberty includes economic liberty.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The dividend is unconditional and equal.

class-collaboration.rationale: George argued labor and capital share common interest against rent.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Opposes sacrificing inheritance; liberal conservation of property.

ban-interest.rationale: George treated interest as a legitimate return to capital, unlike rent.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Law of equal liberty rejects racial classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not a theme; government seen as potentially captured by landowners though.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Severance charges apply to depletion but no stance on expansion.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim has no basis in the sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Government protects rights and is funded by rent, though Foldvary also funds local public goods, so not strictly night-watchman.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Paine and Georgist natural birthright claim equal shares of land.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources treat land rights through rent and use, not the colonial character of particular states, so adherents are unspecified.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Equal liberty protects freedom of belief and practice, so laws limiting religious conversion would be rejected.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Locke and Paine grounds, and geoanarchism ties membership to voluntary consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aim rejected by free-trade outlook.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Law of equal liberty and libertarian non-aggression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cooperation and exchange emphasized, not struggle between peoples.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Paine framed ground rent as justice for the poor, but no priority principle is stated.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: George held land monopoly, not population, causes poverty.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rights are primary under equal liberty.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Opposes aggressive wars but no doctrine.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Charging rent for land use is central, and renting is permitted.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is not covered by the sources, and libertarians differ on state-run schooling.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not part of doctrine; state role in curricula opposed.

minority-language-support.rationale: State language support not part of limited government.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: George held political freedom needs land reform.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty is the ideology's first principle, so trading it for development is rejected.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Historical claims do not ground land rights for George.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Paine and George make property in land conditional on rent to community, but produced property is absolute.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Rights-protecting limited state; also opposes curbing property.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Voluntary secession is a feature of geoanarchism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Prefers abolishing income tax entirely, so a flat tax is a partial improvement.

character-from-environment.rationale: George blamed institutions for poverty but the statement is broader.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule of law and equal liberty mean rulers are bound by law, as Paine and Locke held.

land-redistribution.rationale: George proposed collecting rent without dispossession rather than redistributing plots.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion violates equal liberty and freedom of conscience, so it is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelling dress by law violates individual liberty, which the law of equal liberty forbids.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: George emphasised land institutions and justice, not general materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: George thought monopolies mainly come from land and privilege; antitrust is not proposed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Armed revolt by a small group initiates force, conflicting with the non-aggression principle, so it is rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Paine opposes hereditary privilege; George attacks land aristocracy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: George held depressions recur without land reform; unclear.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Exploitation located in land rent, not imperial extraction.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paine said justice, not charity, and no duty doctrine appears.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Exploitation attributed to land monopoly and trade barriers.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving office by birth contradicts equal rights before the law that the ideology upholds.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist question with no bearing on geolibertarian doctrine.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demanding territory by war or threat would initiate force, which non-aggression rules out.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Giving political rank by descent contradicts equal rights under law, which the ideology treats as central.

paid-care-work.rationale: State-recognized wage pay not part of doctrine.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Rent payment, not nationality, defines claim.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Equal law without regard to outcomes.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Funding foreign fighters is intervention abroad, which the non-aggression and limited-government stance opposes.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Using troops against an ally's government is aggression, which the non-aggression principle rules out.

residents-only-property.rationale: Open land market; geo-rent applies to all.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Voluntary consent view but sources split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities have no basis in the sources and contradict equal rights.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion contradicts equal rights regardless of belief.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Foldvary funds local goods from local geo-rent.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: Land and natural resources common rather than just means of production.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Foldvary favors voluntary private associations partly replacing government services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religious truth claims are outside the doctrine; George and Paine were theists of differing kinds.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary allowed but common property in all goods rejected.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: George saw his scheme as beyond both, but libertarians vary.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Land claims rest on use and rent, not history.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious doctrine not part of the ideology.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The ideology claims to combine libertarian and Georgist views.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist alienation is not a theme; George held labor is deprived by rent not by capitalist production.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Equal liberty and equal rights regardless of belief mean no religion is deemed incompatible with a free society.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Geoanarchists may use private defense; mainstream keeps defense.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law with equal liberty.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marriage across faiths is a private choice protected by equal liberty, so legal restriction is rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Discriminatory boycotts conflict with the equal moral worth that the tradition upholds, though boycotts are legal; rejected.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: George held land monopoly concentrates wealth and subjugates labor.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State promotion of any belief violates neutrality and freedom of conscience, which the ideology upholds.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Only geoanarchists would privatize; mainstream keeps protection.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Paine insists on justice not charity, while libertarians favor voluntary aid.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land is treated as a common inheritance, but holders keep secure possession and title while paying rent rather than holding only while using it.

property-franchise.rationale: Equal natural rights and equal birthright in land mean no property qualification for voting.

rent-control.rationale: Georgists hold that price caps worsen shortages; the remedy is collecting land rent and freeing building so supply rises.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Libertarian non-aggression and voluntary association rule out compulsory state youth organisations.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Georgists hold that land rent is unearned and belongs to the community, while wages and the product of labour are earned; interest on capital is generally accepted.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The non-aggression principle permits defensive force, so absolute pacifism is rejected.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Free markets and equal land rights for all people reject reserving economic roles for a national majority.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Foldvary funds local public goods from land rent but accepts private or voluntary provision; the strand is split.

person-over-state.rationale: Geolibertarianism is built on libertarian non-aggression and self-ownership, so persons are never mere means.

free-public-college.rationale: Libertarian limited government rejects tax-funded tuition, and geolibertarians would fund only minimal government from land rent, with any dividend paid in cash.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Geolibertarians hold that those who use or degrade common natural resources owe the community their rental value, and Foldvary advocates pollution fees alongside land rent in place of regulation.

capital-controls.rationale: Free markets and free movement of goods and capital are core to the libertarian framework, so state control of capital flows is rejected.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Georgists favour free trade and treat land as a common inheritance globally, but have no program for favouring developing countries.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Geoanarchists and Foldvary favour voluntary communities competing with different arrangements, but most geolibertarians share a fixed blueprint of land-value taxation within a market economy.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Land and natural resources are a common inheritance whose rental value is collected and reflected in public finance.

farm-price-support.rationale: Free markets and limited government exclude state price guarantees and public purchase; land rent, not subsidies, funds the commons.

ban-fgm.rationale: Non-aggression forbids physical harm to non-consenting people, including children, so such cutting would be prohibited.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal self-ownership and equal claims to land follow from Paine and George, so women hold land on the same terms.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Liberty is the core principle, though the commons is protected through rent charges rather than by overriding freedoms.

premarital-sex.rationale: Libertarian non-aggression and individual liberty make consensual sex a private matter.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Libertarian non-aggression and free-speech principles oppose government cutting communications.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal individual rights are central to the libertarian framework, which applies to women and men alike.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Locke's first-claim rule is the starting point, but Paine, George and Foldvary hold that land and resources are a common inheritance on which holders owe rent, so first claiming does not give full ownership.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Geolibertarians pair free markets with a minimal state and reject a state-planned economy, so defending one runs against the core program.

national-church-status.rationale: A limited-government libertarian framework gives no state privileges to any church, and voluntary association is the model.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Non-aggression and due process in a limited-government libertarian framework rule out killing suspects without trial.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The core Georgist and geolibertarian claim is that land and resources are a common inheritance and holders owe the community their rental value.

self-ownership.rationale: Geolibertarianism is a libertarian doctrine: people own themselves and what their labour produces.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Land rent is meant to replace taxes on labour, goods and income, so consumption taxes are to be abolished.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Land monopoly is treated as a state-backed privilege to be ended, and libertarians oppose special legal privileges for firms.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: They favor replacing bureaucratic welfare with an unconditional rent dividend, so adherents are split on simply cutting. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Land and natural resources belong equally to all people, and those who hold them should pay the community for exclusive use.
missingStatements.rationale: Paine, George and Foldvary all ground the program in a common birthright to land, which no existing statement captures directly.

missingStatements.text: Polluters and those who deplete natural resources should pay charges to the community.
missingStatements.rationale: Geolibertarians add pollution and severance charges to land rent as payment for use of the shared commons.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow charge mechanism; already part of the land-rent and commons logic of land-value-tax, and few other ideologies split on it.

notes: Strands split on whether government is needed: mainstream geolibertarians keep a minimal rent-funded state, while geoanarchists use private agencies. Many low-confidence answers are inferred from libertarian principles, since sources discuss land and tax policy almost exclusively.
